the survival of breast cancer patients with lymph node metastases is significantly better if there is no change in expression of the markers HER2, ER, and PR between the primary tumor and the lymph node metastases, or if there is a change towards a more favorable expression.

the expression of the markers studied in the primary tumor and the lymph node metastasis of breast cancer patients is not associated with the survival time, except in the case of the expression of the HER2 marker in the lymph node metastases of patients with HER2-negative primary tumors.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the survival of breast cancer patients with lymph node metastases is dependent on the expression of selected markers in the metastases.
the expression of the selected markers in the lymph node metastases does not seem to be of prognostic value in breast cancer.

the expression of HER2 in the primary tumor is not a prognostic factor in the lymph node-negative breast cancer patients, but in the lymph node-positive patients the expression of HER-2 is associated with a worse outcome.
